name: Grepafloxacin

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in United States and 5 other countries, first in 1999 — for heart harm

summary: Grepafloxacin was pulled from the market in the United States and five other countries starting in 1999 because of heart harm [3]. Based on a small computer model rather than tests on people, the drug received a high score of 85 for liver concerns and a low score of 6 for heart concerns [M]. Several similar drugs also have serious warnings or were removed from the market due to nerve, muscle, bone, blood, metabolic, or heart harms [4][5][6]. Additionally, one clinical trial involving the drug stopped early because of low patient enrollment and staffing shortages [8].
